text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike of CUTLASS fallbacks for models we usually route to Triton during KV coldstart on H100/seq64. 99th latency jumped ~120ms on a few user flows. pattern: small batches (1-3), KV miss on first token -> Triton starts, then arbiter switches to CUTLASS mid-request.
sam: ugh. is the arbiter using latency_estimates only or also memory/kv_state?
maria: looks like the decider flips when observed mem_alloc > threshold after kv fill. the sequence-length bias is causing oscillation on the hotpath.
aj: can you paste a stack/profile snippet? want to see where the switch is triggered.
maria: paste from trace (trimmed):
```
ARB_DECIDE: prefer=triton score=0.95 kv_bias=-0.12 mem_est=720MB latency_est=18ms -> choose TRITON
KV_MISS on token1 -> kv_populate + buffer_growth -> mem_est=980MB latency_est=40ms -> choose CUTLASS fallback at token4
```
aj: that gap (18ms -> 40ms) is the problem. if arbiter recomputes per-token we get thrash. suggest adding a grace window or hysteresis so once a kernel is picked it stays for Xms or tokens.
leo: +1 to hysteresis. also think KV coldstart should add a negative bias to CUTLASS preference (i.e., favor Triton while kv warms). CUTLASS seems better for steady-state but not for the first few tokens.
sam: propose config experiment: add 'kv_cold_bias' and 'stickiness_ms' to kernel_arbiter and a flag to route on batch_size for first N tokens. e.g.:
```
kernel_arbiter:
  preference_weights:
    triton: 1.0
    cutlass: 1.0
  kv_cold_bias: -0.35    # negative favors triton during kv coldstart
  stickiness_ms: 50      # keep chosen kernel for at least 50ms
  per_token_evaluate: true
  per_token_min_interval_ms: 25
```
perf-bot: new perf run queued: https://perf.example/runs/2063045678 (includes nvprof traces + latency histograms) :bar_chart:
maria: thanks, i'll attach correlation of KV miss tags to the traces. initial look shows most oscillations happen when batch_size <= 2 and seq_len <= 64.
aj: another angle: detect 'kv_fill_in_progress' and mark decision immutable until kv_ready flag flips. simpler than time-based hysteresis.
sam: good idea. but need fallback safety — if memory skyrockets or OOM risk, we still want to switch. add an escape hatch: force-switch if mem_est > mem_soft_limit or if latency_est > latency_slo * 3.
leo: agree. maybe also prefer preemptive sampling: probe a small fraction of requests with the alternate kernel (1%) and collect steady-state counters to update preference_weights. keep probes tagged so they don't affect SLOs.
maria: i'll run two experiments: (A) stickiness_ms=50 + kv_cold_bias=-0.35; (B) kv_immutable_flag approach with escape hatch thresholds. will post results tomorrow.
aj: for the experiment, log these fields on decision events: chosen_kernel, prev_kernel, mem_est, latency_est, kv_state, batch_size, seq_len. also include trace_id so we can link to nvprof.
maria: will do. sample line in decision log: `DECIDE trace=abc123 chosen=triton prev=none mem=720MB lat=18ms kv=cold batch=1 seq=16`.
sam: if experiment (A) reduces 99th by >30ms and removes mid-request switches, ship as default for H100 seq64 for now.
perf-bot: experiment A results: 99p latency down 38ms, fallback events down 82% (run 2063045678-A).
maria: wow that's promising. scheduling rollout canary on 10% of traffic for next 24h. tagging eng-oncall.
leo: document the calibration knobs in runtime/arbiter/README so SREs can tweak without code deploy. small config bump only.
aj: note to future self: re-evaluate when we enable larger batch prefetching — may change mem_est behavior.
maria: thanks all, will push config PR with flags and perf dashboard links. :thumbsup:
